steps.content: At Brock's grave, Dravyn found the missing youngest daughter of the Andohar family.
Her gaze was fixed upon the headstone, yet seemed to look through it, reaching toward the distant front lines. In response, a rare gentleness softened Dravyn's hardened demeanor.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: The Andohar family... Your father sent emissaries. Very generous terms. They say the head of the Andohar family will come himself next time. To bring you home.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Aren't you going to meet them?
She turned around and opened her mouth, speaking with impeccable "propriety."

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Are you trying to trick me, you old grouch? You'd never let me leave. I know too much. I'd be dead before I took one step past the gate.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Not here. You'll have Brock climbing out of his grave to scold you.
Catherine let out a soft giggle, her expression easing slightly.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: My father knows I don't want to go home right now. He's just using this as an excuse to meet you, Commander of the Independence Army.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Let me guess... has the Andohar family already made you a weapons offer? They must think you're desperate. Perfect time to make a deal.
Dravyn merely shrugged, a silent confirmation. Before Brock's tombstone, the two fell into another shared, weighty silence.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Brock said he didn't want me on the battlefield... But I'd already seen plenty of wars.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I've been in a private airship of the metropoles, flying over settlements they were pacifying.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I watched from the VIP cabin as bombs fell like hail. The people below held their makeshift weapons, refusing to surrender even in the face of death.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Though the weapons on both sides came from my family. So we always knew how it would end.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: The budget difference, the tech gap, the training quality... The strong and the weak are objective, irreversible facts. The metropoles know it. That's why they don't care about the arms dealers' little games, but...

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: But those people down there... they still cling to this hope. That the weapons they bought might hold some miracle. That it could suddenly turn the war, make all the stubborn dying mean something.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Unfortunately, I've never once seen that miracle happen.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Are you saying our resistance is foolish?
She avoided answering directly, changing the subject instead.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: The Tide of Ashes will thin by mid-September. That's the metropoles' window. Their bombers will get through. Even with refueling and maintenance...

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: By October at the latest, you'll face a second nuclear strike. This time, they'll be aiming at DisCity.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Do you understand what that means?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: ...I do.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Your Independence Army can't stop it. Not as you are now.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: I know.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: So what's your plan? Even if you placed an order with the Andohars today for nukes, it'd be too late. You can't threaten all five metropoles at once.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Your troops are already losing faith, aren't they? Brock's gone, and your stubbornness alone isn't enough to hold them together.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: You're right. We're fighting an uphill battle.
She looked at the gravestone again. This time, there was more than one surrounding them.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: If you surrender now, a lot of people would be relieved. They might even thank you for that. Even Helena and Brock wouldn't blame you, not after all this.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: ...Except me. The annoying Andohar brat.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Don't you surrender, Dravyn. I've seen people with their backs against the wall—outnumbered, outgunned, still fighting while knowing all too well that they're weak.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I want to see them win. I want to join the fight and help them win. Beating impossible odds—that's the kind of victory that matters the most.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: So fight harder. Think smarter. Weren't you supposed to be the stubborn one? If even you are thinking about giving up... then hand your command to me. I'll lead the fight myself!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Surrender isn't in my vocabulary. And yes, I'm not letting you go back, but not because I don't trust you. You wouldn't betray us.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: You said you wanted to join the fight. That you were the ultimate weapon. I never forgot that.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: My superpowers? I've told you, my range is less than ten meters. Sending me against nukes would just get your soldiers killed.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Desperation isn't a strategy, General. You're supposed to be the pragmatist here. Use your brain. Don't send me on a suicide mission.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: So you'll fight... if I can give you a real shot at winning. Is that right?

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: ...If your plan actually has a chance? Then fine. I suppose I could take orders from you.
Dravyn broke into a smile.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Haven't you figured me out already?
He took one final look at the gravestone, rose to his feet, and fastened his military cap.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: I'm not like Brock. I have no lines I won't cross. No cost is too high if it leads to victory.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: DisCity belongs to us. And now that I'm in command, I'm not giving it up.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: The victory I want will come, one way or another.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: So wait here. Those game-changing weapons you've been waiting for? I'll bring them to you very soon.

???: It's been a while. Are you still using the prototype I gave you?
Dravyn: Brock told me it works well. But it doesn't last long.
???: There are other organizations in this world conducting similar experiments, but that power they're dealing with is extremely dangerous.
???: They're carving out spaces beneath ancient and modern battlefields, using some kind of substance to create abnormal weapons.

Dravyn: You've helped us greatly in the past. Your abilities have been invaluable to both the Independence Army and all of DisCity.
EDGE Intern: My loyalty is to humanity. The world Keylan left behind shouldn't be defiled this way.
